title: SSSD Authentication Failure After SLES 15 SP7 Update | SUSE | Support Center
plain_text:
SSSD Authentication Failure After SLES 15 SP7 Update
Environment
Help Environment

SLES 15 SP7
SSSD 2.10
Active Directory LDAP

Situation
Problem

After updating packages on a system running SLES 15 SP7, external authentication via SSSD to Active Directory fails. Users can only log in with local accounts.

Steps to Reproduce
Update packages on a system running SLES 15 SP7, which includes an update to SSSD version 2.10.
Attempt to authenticate against Active Directory via SSSD.
Observe that authentication fails, and users can only log in with local accounts.
Observed Behavior

SSSD logs show connection problems to the LDAP server, indicating "Invalid credentials" and "Authentication Failed".

Specific log entries include:

ldap_sasl_interactive_bind_s failed (49) Invalid credentials
Unable to establish connection 1432158227 : Authentication Failed
Extended failure message: 80090346: LdapErr: DSID-0C0906F9, comment: AcceptSecurityContext error, data 80090346

Initially, attempts to restart SSSD after clearing caches might also fail with messages like:

Failed to bind socket "/var/lib/sss/pipes/private/sbus-master": Datei oder Verzeichnis nicht gefunden

The command 'sssctl domain-status <domain_name>' reports "Online status: Offline".

Resolution

1. Edit the SSSD configuration file '/etc/sssd/sssd.conf'. Ensure that 'ldap_id_use_start_tls' is set to 'true' (this is the default for SSSD 2.10 and newer, but verify).

# Example entry in /etc/sssd/sssd.conf under the domain section
ldap_id_use_start_tls = true

2. Create or modify the global LDAP client configuration file, typically '/etc/openldap/ldap.conf'. 

3. Add the following lines to the chosen LDAP client configuration file to configure SASL channel binding properties:

SASL_CBINDING   tls-endpoint
SASL_SECPROPS   minssf=0 maxssf=0

4. Restart the SSSD service:

systemctl restart sssd.service

7. Verify the SSSD domain status to confirm it is online:

sssctl domain-status <domain_name>
Cause
Primary Cause

The primary cause of the authentication failure is a change in the default behavior of SSSD version 2.10 (introduced with SLES 15 SP7 packages). The parameter 'ldap_id_use_start_tls' changed its default value from 'false' to 'true' for improved security. While SSSD successfully negotiates the StartTLS connection, the subsequent SASL/GSSAPI bind to Active Directory fails because SSSD does not correctly provide the necessary LDAP Channel Binding Tokens (CBT) when the bind occurs inside a TLS channel.

Active Directory, with modern security defaults, expects these binding tokens to prevent Man-In-The-Middle attacks. The absence or incorrect handling of CBTs by the underlying SASL library causes Active Directory to reject the bind with an "Invalid credentials" (error 49) and an "AcceptSecurityContext error" (data 80090346), even when the Kerberos credentials (keytabs, tickets) are otherwise valid.

Additional Information
Secure LDAP Connection Best Practices

For a fully secure LDAP connection with `ldap_id_use_start_tls = true`, ensure the Root-CA certificate of the Active Directory Domain is imported into the system's trust store. Copy the Root-CA certificate to `/etc/pki/trust/anchors` and update the certificate database:

cp <root_ca_certificate.crt> /etc/pki/trust/anchors/
update-ca-certificates'

This prevents unencrypted LDAP connections and ensures that SSSD can validate the TLS certificate provided by the Active Directory server.
